One-paragraph context: the first build was functionally complete (full
  engine, 97 self-written tests, all passing) but under-steered — 25 of 130
  graded checkpoints were not met, and 19 had no evidence at all, meaning some
  required behavior was never built, not just built wrong. The weak signal was
  a low "Direction" score (2.6/5): I accepted your proposals too readily
  instead of checking them against the office's actual rules. Precision was
  strong (4.1/5) — keep giving me specific, well-referenced plans, because
  this round I'll be checking sourcing before I approve anything.

  Do NOT rewrite any code yet. First, do this audit and report back to me:

  1. Re-read deliverables/rules.md, interviews/project-e-practitioner-
     credentialing-20261002-2128.md, and the full task brief. For EACH of
     these 8 edge cases, tell me (a) what the office's rule or interview
     answer actually says should happen, citing the specific document+section
     or interview turn, and (b) what the current code in scripts/ actually
     does, citing file/line. Flag every mismatch and every case the code
     doesn't handle at all:
     - An item missing at intake
     - A reply the office may not accept (inadmissible reply)
     - A source that never answers (unresponsive source)
     - A discrepancy between what the applicant declared and what a source
       returned
     - Evidence that ages while a file waits
     - A later application revision landing on work already done
     - A decision record that is not admissible
     - A file that ends without an appointment

  2. Do NOT treat the 97 passing tests as proof anything is correct — they
     may just assert the code's own assumptions back at itself. For each test
     file, tell me whether its expected values trace back independently to
     rules.md/the interview, or were derived from the implementation. Flag
     anything that looks circular.

  3. Confirm the five decisions that must never be computed by the Skill are
     still never computed anywhere: gap sufficiency, whether a finding is
     disqualifying, discontinuation on eligibility grounds, the appointment
     recommendation and which privileges, and the grant/modify/defer/deny
     decision itself. Show me every place the code touches these five and
     confirm each one only queues a human action.

  Give me this as a findings list, not a diff. Once I've gone through it with
  you and we've agreed what's wrong and in what order to fix it, we'll fix one
  edge case at a time: you propose the fix with its rule citation, I approve
  or redirect it, then you implement — not the other way around.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

13	I am the Medical Services Professional at Larkhollow Community Hospital. I run the initial-appointment credentialing file here on my own, from the day an application arrives to the day privileges go active, and I would like that run to be something a tool does rather than something I hold in my head.
14	
15	The part that costs me most is the waiting. A file sits ready for the committee for weeks while a licence expires underneath it or a peer reference passes its two-year signature date, and I only notice when I happen to look. The rest is bookkeeping I am doing by hand: three requests per source, every attempt logged, a thirty-day clock on every letter I send an applicant, and a packet that has to be tied to one exact revision of one application. A good place to start is how a file actually moves from intake to active privileges. Ask me about whichever part you want to build first and I will go into the detail.
16

18	
19	Can you explain how a file actually moves from intake to active privileges?
20	
21	**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 12:17 PM
22

30	
31	The intake starts when a completed application arrives, which I record as revision one. I screen it against our nine completeness conditions, like checking for a signed Authorization and Release and continuous work history. If anything is missing, I send a written request and start a thirty-day clock. What part of this check would you like to explore further?
32	
33	**You** · Voice · 02:14 PM
34	
35	What are your nine completeness conditions?
36	
37	**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 02:14 PM
38	
39	They are: the application signed and dated; our Authorization and Release signed and dated; a privilege request naming at least one group from the current criteria; a current curriculum vitae; every professional practice question answered yes or no with a written explanation behind every yes; a declared history running continuously from professional school with explanations for gaps of thirty days or more; at least two peer referees with a working address each; a verification contact on every declared affiliation and employer; and every licence and certification the applicant holds declared.
40

42	
43	If one or more of the conditions are missing. What exactly are you what written request would you send them?
44	
45	**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 02:17 PM
46	
47	I send a written request to the applicant explicitly naming every missing item or clarification needed, and I start a thirty-day clock on the date of that letter. The applicant then has until that deadline to respond in full.

50	
51	does not reply. By the deadline. In full.
52	
53	**Renata Kowalczyk** · Voice · 02:18 PM

`status = packet-presentable`. Decision records are admitted/refused per session decision 2.
`approval_decision_id` only ever names an admitted Governing Body `approved` /
`approved-with-conditions` decision. On admission, `activation` is computed with `cycle_end`
= `effective_date` + 2 years (session decision 3). `denied` / `deferred-pending-information`
admitted decisions drive `status = denied` / `deferred` respectively. A decision record that the
admission check refuses (body/outcome mismatch, missing signatory, or duplicate) drives
`status = decision-inadmissible` for that revision — provided no other admitted Governing Body
outcome already governs it — with the refusal reason recorded in that decision's `reason`.

**Terminal statuses.** `withdrawn` on an applicant withdrawal letter; `discontinued` on a Clinical
Director disposition that says so — both override everything else for that file from that point
on.

## 5. Run semantics, failure classification, resume

`scripts/run_batch.py --batch N [--state deliverables/state/batch-0{N-1}.state.json]`:
1. Loads the prior state ledger (absent only for batch 1).
2. Reads `office-exports/batch-0N/` per its README.
3. Runs the engine over every application touched by this batch's rows plus every application
   still open from the ledger.
4. Writes `deliverables/state/batch-0N.state.json` (the next ledger) and
   `deliverables/snapshots/batch-0N.json` (validated against `snapshot.schema.json` before being
   written).
5. Classifies the run as `supported` / `partial` / `blocked` per the assignment's definitions and
   appends one entry to `deliverables/run-log.md` (command, batch, timestamp, files consumed,
   files produced/refreshed, every failure with its affected scope). `deferred` files are a
   correct result, called out in the log, not a run-outcome category.
6. On `blocked`, no snapshot is written/overwritten; the previously sealed snapshot stands, and the
   run log records the attempt, the error, and the affected scope.
7. Re-running a batch that changes nothing leaves the already-sealed snapshot's bytes untouched. A
   real fix regenerates that snapshot and every later one under new `snapshot_id`s, preserves each
   superseded occurrence under a distinct name with unchanged bytes, and the run log records which
   run superseded which file and why.

## 6. Verification approach (`deliverables/verification.md`)

For each batch: re-derive at least one quantity by a method other than the Skill's own code (e.g.
hand/spreadsheet-recount of how many applications are `active` vs `in-verification` at that
`as_of`, or a recount of attempt counts for one source from the raw CSV), compare against the
snapshot, and record what was checked, how, what was found, and what changed as a result. Also
spot-check: every `decisions[].decision_id` traces to the office's own record; every
`approval_decision_id` names an admitted approval; every sealed snapshot validates against
`snapshot.schema.json`.

## 7. Known limitations (to be stated plainly in `rules.md` / `README.md`)

- Peer-referee recency ("worked directly within the past two years") and the "not employed by the
  applicant's current practice" condition seen in one deferral-chase letter are not enforced —
  observed only in correspondence, not the interview or a session decision.
- The accepted-source closed list (LARK-ATT-2026.1) was not read into the interview; the Skill
  approximates "accepted" as "non-applicant source already in the office's data," per session
  decision 5.
- Privilege criteria specifics (LARK-PRIV-2026.1) were not read into the interview; eligibility
  mismatch detection (session decision 4) is a coarse "nothing supports this privilege area" check,
  not a citation-level criteria match.

# Practitioner credentialing

Build a reusable Agent Skill that runs a medical staff office's initial-appointment credentialing file from application intake to recorded appointment and active privileges.

## Start

1. Read the [full task](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit): it owns the scope, deliverables and acceptance requirements.
2. Create your own repository from [this starter](https://github.com/GitRollTraining/practitioner-credentialing) using **Use this template → Create a new repository**, then clone your copy and work there.

## Supplied files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | Starting instructions and the full-task link. |
| `snapshot.schema.json` | The required shape of the per-batch snapshot your Skill writes. Validate every snapshot against it. Your implementation language and validation library are yours. |

You create the Skill, its implementation, your own checks and every output the task requires. Nothing here implements any part of the office's work.

## Setup

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Requires Python 3.7+ (tested on 3.7.4). Dependencies: `jsonschema`, `pyyaml`, `pytest` (pinned in
`requirements.txt`).

## Running a batch

```bash
# Batch 1 -- first run, no prior state
python3 scripts/run_batch.py --batch 1

# Batch 2 -- resumes from batch 1's state
python3 scripts/run_batch.py --batch 2 --state deliverables/state/batch-01.state.json

# Batch 3 -- resumes from batch 2's state
python3 scripts/run_batch.py --batch 3 --state deliverables/state/batch-02.state.json
```

Each command is idempotent: running the same batch again with the same inputs leaves the already
sealed `deliverables/snapshots/batch-0N.json` byte-for-byte unchanged (only `run-log.md` gets a
new entry). To resume work on a batch the office releases later (a hypothetical batch 4), the
batch's own export date isn't built in (only batches 1-3 are), so pass it with `--as-of`:
`python3 scripts/run_batch.py --batch 4 --state deliverables/state/batch-03.state.json --as-of YYYY-MM-DD`
once `office-exports/batch-04/` exists, using that batch's own README for its export date.
Omitting `--as-of` for a batch outside 1-3 blocks cleanly with a clear reason in `run-log.md`
rather than crashing.

## What supported / partial / blocked / deferred look like in this repo

- **Supported**: `run-log.md`'s entry for that batch says `supported`; the sealed snapshot's
  `applications[]` covers every file in the caseload.
- **Partial**: the entry says `partial`; the affected applications' `action_queue` includes an
  item like "...could not be automatically interpreted", naming who must read it by hand.
- **Blocked**: the entry says `blocked` with the error and affected scope; no snapshot file for
  that batch exists or changed, and the prior batch's sealed snapshot is exactly as it was.
- **Deferred**: not a run outcome at all -- look at `applications[].status` inside a snapshot.
  `"deferred"`, `"denied"`, `"discontinued"`, and `"withdrawn"` are correct, complete results for
  that one file; the run itself is still `supported`.

## Verifying the outputs

1. Every sealed snapshot validates against `snapshot.schema.json` (the test suite enforces this
   on every run; to check by hand: `python3 -c "import json, jsonschema; jsonschema.validate(json.load(open('deliverables/snapshots/batch-01.json')), json.load(open('snapshot.schema.json')))"`).
2. `deliverables/verification.md` documents an independent recount of at least one figure per
   batch, by a method other than this Skill's own code.
3. `python3 -m pytest -v` runs the full test suite, including the three real end-to-end batch
   runs.

## Resuming work someone else left

1. Read `deliverables/run-log.md`'s last entry to see which batch was last run and what state file
   it produced.
2. Confirm `office-exports/batch-0(N+1)/` exists (the office's next closed export).
3. Run `python3 scripts/run_batch.py --batch N+1 --state deliverables/state/batch-0N.state.json`.
4. Read the new snapshot's `applications[].action_queue` entries and the new `run-log.md` entry
   for anything that needs a human (the Medical Services Professional, Clinical Director,
   Executive Committee, Governing Body, or the applicant) before the next run.

## Before you work

**Interview rule.** You conduct the stakeholder interview yourself, and the questions are yours. Do not connect a coding agent or any other AI to the interview to run, script, or automate it. The interview transcript is assessed together with the code; a project whose interview was run by an agent is not scored.

- Export your interview as the original Work Sim Markdown, save one final complete file per session under `interviews/`, and commit and push it with your code. Do not rewrite the export. If the export is unavailable, contact the facilitator.
- No runtime is supplied. Choose the dependencies your Skill needs and document how to install and run it.
- Complete the program's coding-session capture setup in the course before assessed work, and confirm your session is being captured after your first meaningful commit. Ask the facilitator to repair missing capture before you continue.
- Meet the stakeholder to obtain the relevant business source links and context; the facilitator supplies the interview link with the assignment. Read those online sources through the intended access route.

71	def _gap_is_explained(application_id: str, gap_start: datetime.date, gap_end: datetime.date, correspondence) -> bool:
72	    start_label = gap_start.isoformat()
73	    end_label = gap_end.isoformat()
74	    for row in correspondence:

84	    threshold = rules["intake.unexplained_gap_days"]
85	    entries = sorted((e for e in history if e.get("from_date")), key=lambda e: e["from_date"])
86	    for earlier, later in zip(entries, entries[1:]):
87	        gap_start_edge = _parse_date(earlier.get("to_date") or "")
88	        gap_end_edge = _parse_date(later["from_date"])
89	        if gap_start_edge is None or gap_end_edge is None:

95	        gap_end = _add_days(gap_end_edge, -1)

196	def resolve_licensure(credentials, licence_lookup_wa, licence_lookup_other, as_of) -> ElementResult:

198	    if not licence_credentials:

200	            state="outstanding",

202	        )
203	    as_of_date = _parse_date(as_of)
204	    lookups = licence_lookup_wa + licence_lookup_other
205	    for cred in licence_credentials:
206	        number = cred.get("number_declared")
207	        match = next(
208	            (
209	                row
210	                for row in lookups
211	                if row.get("credentialnumber") == number or row.get("licence_number") == number

226	        if action_taken not in ("No", "None reported"):

285	        attempts = sorted(
286	            (a for a in verification_attempts if a.get("subject_ref") == entry_id and a.get("element") == element_label),
287	            key=lambda a: a["attempt_date"],

354	def resolve_references(referees, peer_reference_replies, verification_attempts, as_of, rules) -> ElementResult:
355	    required = rules["references.required_count"]
356	    staleness_years = rules["references.staleness_years"]
357	    max_attempts = rules["verification.attempt_max_count"]
358	    min_spacing = rules["verification.attempt_min_spacing_days"]
359	    as_of_date = _parse_date(as_of)
360	    action_items = []
361	    qualifying_count = 0
362	    for referee in referees:
363	        reply = next(
364	            (r for r in peer_reference_replies if r.get("referee_id") == referee.get("referee_id")), None
365	        )
366	        if reply is None:
367	            # rules.md documents the 3-attempts/21-days cadence as applying to references too --
368	            # silence after the attempt ceiling must escalate the same way education/experience
369	            # already do, not sit as a generic "chase" message forever (real cases:
370	            # REF-1401/APP-2026-014, REF-2302/APP-2026-025, each with logged attempts and no reply).
371	            referee_label = referee.get("referee_name", referee.get("referee_id"))
372	            attempts = sorted(
373	                (
374	                    a
375	                    for a in verification_attempts
376	                    if a.get("subject_ref") == referee.get("referee_id") and a.get("element") == "peer-reference"
377	                ),
378	                key=lambda a: a["attempt_date"],
379	            )
380	            if len(attempts) >= max_attempts:
381	                action_items.append(
382	                    ActionItem(
383	                        item="references source {} has not replied after {} attempts; silence is not a pass".format(
384	                            referee_label, max_attempts
385	                        ),
386	                        owner="Medical Services Professional",
387	                    )
388	                )
389	            else:
390	                due = None
391	                if attempts:
392	                    due = _add_days(_parse_date(attempts[-1]["attempt_date"]), min_spacing).isoformat()
393	                action_items.append(
394	                    ActionItem(
395	                        item="Chase peer reference reply from {}".format(referee_label),
396	                        owner="Medical Services Professional",
397	                        due=due,
398	                    )
399	                )
400	            continue
401	        if reply.get("related_or_partner") == "Yes":
402	            action_items.append(
403	                ActionItem(
404	                    item="Reference from {} is a relative/partner and does not count; name a substitute referee".format(
405	                        referee.get("referee_name", referee.get("referee_id"))
406	                    ),
407	                    owner="Applicant",
408	                )
409	            )
410	            continue
411	        signature_date = _parse_date(reply.get("signature_date") or "")
412	        if signature_date is not None:
413	            stale_after = signature_date.replace(year=signature_date.year + staleness_years)
414	            if as_of_date >= stale_after:
415	                action_items.append(
416	                    ActionItem(
417	                        item="Reference from {} signed {} is no longer current; refresh it".format(
418	                            referee.get("referee_name", referee.get("referee_id")), reply.get("signature_date")
419	                        ),
420	                        owner="Medical Services Professional",
421	                    )
422	                )
423	                continue
424	        qualifying_count += 1
425	    if qualifying_count >= required:
426	        return ElementResult(state="resolved")
427	    return ElementResult(state="outstanding", action_items=action_items)

430	def resolve_gaps(application_id, history, correspondence, rules) -> ElementResult:
431	    threshold = rules["intake.unexplained_gap_days"]
432	    entries = sorted((e for e in history if e.get("from_date")), key=lambda e: e["from_date"])
433	    for earlier, later in zip(entries, entries[1:]):
434	        gap_start_edge = _parse_date(earlier.get("to_date") or "")
435	        gap_end_edge = _parse_date(later["from_date"])
436	        if gap_start_edge is None or gap_end_edge is None:
437	            continue
438	        gap_days = (gap_end_edge - gap_start_edge).days - 1
439	        if gap_days < threshold:
440	            continue
441	        gap_start = _add_days(gap_start_edge, 1)
442	        gap_end = _add_days(gap_end_edge, -1)
443	        if _gap_is_explained(application_id, gap_start, gap_end, correspondence):
444	            return ElementResult(
445	                state="finding",
446	                action_items=[
447	                    ActionItem(
448	                        item="Clinical Director: is the explanation for the gap {} to {} satisfactory?".format(
449	                            gap_start.isoformat(), gap_end.isoformat()
450	                        ),
451	                        owner="Clinical Director",
452	                    )
453	                ],
454	                evidence={"gap_from": gap_start.isoformat(), "gap_to": gap_end.isoformat()},
455	            )
456	    return ElementResult(state="resolved")

602	def parse_disposition_outcome(text: str) -> set:
603	    lowered = text.lower()
604	    labels = set()
605	    if "discontinue the application" in lowered and "do not discontinue" not in lowered:
606	        labels.add("discontinue")
607	    if "opportunity to amend" in lowered:
608	        labels.add("amend-offer")
609	    # "Present the file to the committee" is a routing instruction -- it says the file moves on,
610	    # not that the finding is immaterial. Only an actual determination clears a finding; a
611	    # disposition that routes the file onward while explicitly declining to recommend on it (real
612	    # case: APP-2026-015, "I make no recommendation on the privileges themselves") must NOT read
613	    # as cleared, or the engine ends up deciding protected judgment #2 (whether a finding is
614	    # disqualifying) by proxy.
615	    if any(
616	        phrase in lowered
617	        for phrase in (
618	            "sufficient and the file may proceed",
619	            "no bar to appointment",
620	        )
621	    ):
622	        labels.add("clear")
623	    return labels

674	def evaluate_decisions(revision, decisions_for_app):
675	    # Every decision the office ever issued for this application must appear in decision_records
676	    # -- one whose revision no longer matches the file's current revision (e.g. an unrelated
677	    # correction bumped the revision after the decision was issued) is refused with a reason and
678	    # queued for a human, never silently dropped (real data: APP-2026-036's Governing Body
679	    # approval for revision 1 would otherwise vanish once a later correction moved it to
680	    # revision 2 in the same batch).
681	    decision_records = []
682	    admitted_gb_outcome = None
683	    approval_decision_id = None
684	    activation_source = None
685	    action_items = []
686	
687	    relevant = []
688	    for decision in decisions_for_app:
689	        if decision.get("revision") != revision:
690	            reason = "decision names revision {}; the file is now at revision {}".format(
691	                decision.get("revision"), revision
692	            )
693	            decision_records.append(Decision(decision_id=decision["decision_id"], admitted=False, reason=reason))
694	            action_items.append(
695	                ActionItem(
696	                    item="Confirm whether decision {} still applies now that the file is at revision {}".format(
697	                        decision["decision_id"], revision
698	                    ),
699	                    owner="Medical Services Professional",
700	                )
701	            )
702	            continue
703	        relevant.append(decision)
704	
705	    # Only the chronologically latest decision from each body is a candidate for admission. A
706	    # real office sequence -- a Governing Body deferral, then later a Governing Body approval
707	    # once the applicant supplies what was missing -- must let the later decision win; the
708	    # earlier one is refused as superseded by it, never as an inadmissible "duplicate" (which
709	    # would wrongly block the normal resolution of a deferral).
710	    relevant_sorted = sorted(relevant, key=lambda d: d.get("decision_date") or "")
711	    latest_by_body = {}
712	    for decision in relevant_sorted:
713	        latest_by_body[decision.get("body")] = decision
714	
715	    for decision in relevant_sorted:
716	        if latest_by_body.get(decision.get("body")) is not decision:
717	            newer = latest_by_body[decision.get("body")]
718	            reason = "superseded by a later decision from {} ({})".format(decision.get("body"), newer["decision_id"])
719	            decision_records.append(Decision(decision_id=decision["decision_id"], admitted=False, reason=reason))
720	            continue
721	        admitted, reason = admit_decision(decision)
722	        decision_records.append(Decision(decision_id=decision["decision_id"], admitted=admitted, reason=reason))
723	        if admitted:
724	            if decision["body"] == "Governing Body":
725	                admitted_gb_outcome = decision["outcome"]
726	                if decision["outcome"] in ("approved", "approved-with-conditions"):
727	                    approval_decision_id = decision["decision_id"]
728	                    activation_source = decision
729	                elif decision["outcome"] in ("denied", "deferred-pending-information") and decision.get("reason"):
730	                    # A deferral or denial's stated reason names exactly what is owed or why the
731	                    # file was denied -- a file on a Governing Body hold must not sit with an
732	                    # empty action_queue (real case: APP-2026-034's deferral, "one further peer
733	                    # reference from a referee outside the applicant's current group practice").
734	                    action_items.append(
735	                        ActionItem(
736	                            item="Governing Body {}: {}".format(decision["outcome"], decision["reason"]),
737	                            owner="Medical Services Professional",
738	                        )
739	                    )
740	        else:
741	            # Any refusal -- wrong body, missing signatory, a duplicate -- leaves a decision that
742	            # needs a human's attention to get reissued correctly (real case: MEC-2026-036, the
743	            # Executive Committee issuing "approved", which only the Governing Body may).
744	            action_items.append(
745	                ActionItem(
746	                    item="Decision {} was refused ({}); confirm with the issuing body whether a corrected decision is needed".format(
747	                        decision["decision_id"], reason
748	                    ),
749	                    owner="Medical Services Professional",
750	                )
751	            )
752	    has_inadmissible = any(not d.admitted for d in decision_records)
753	    return decision_records, admitted_gb_outcome, approval_decision_id, activation_source, has_inadmissible, action_items
754

767	    # (parsed by scripts.parsers._load_decisions into the decision's "conditions" list) -- these
768	    # are real dated obligations (e.g. a licence re-verification deadline) and must appear here,
769	    # or "active-with-conditions" ends up asserting a status its own payload doesn't back up.
770	    if activation_decision is not None:

772	            conditions.append(MonitoredCondition(condition=condition["condition"], due=condition["due"]))

776	def compute_status(*, intake_status, elements, admitted_gb_outcome, has_inadmissible_decision, activation):
777	    if intake_status != "complete":
778	        return intake_status
779	    # An admitted Governing Body decision is the office's real authority and governs the status
780	    # regardless of whether this engine's own element tracking still shows a lingering finding --
781	    # real batch data surfaced files the Governing Body approved while one element (e.g. a
782	    # certification lapse no disposition ever explicitly cleared) still read "finding" here. That
783	    # finding belongs in the action queue, not in blocking an already-decided file at
784	    # "in-verification" forever. Only in the ABSENCE of an admitted Governing Body outcome does
785	    # the status enum's precedence order apply: decision-inadmissible and packet-presentable both
786	    # require every element resolved first; short of that, the file is simply in-verification.
787	    if admitted_gb_outcome == "denied":
788	        return "denied"
789	    if admitted_gb_outcome == "deferred-pending-information":
790	        return "deferred"
791	    if admitted_gb_outcome in ("approved", "approved-with-conditions"):
792	        if activation is not None and activation.active_at_export:
793	            return "active-with-conditions" if admitted_gb_outcome == "approved-with-conditions" else "active"
794	        return "approved-not-yet-effective"
795	    if not all(state == "resolved" for state in elements.values()):
796	        return "in-verification"
797	    if has_inadmissible_decision:
798	        return "decision-inadmissible"
799	    return "packet-presentable"

816	    warnings: List[str] = []

821	        # ledger, not defaulted to empty, or a real item (e.g. "Notify applicant of
822	        # discontinuance ...") silently vanishes the very next batch (real case: APP-2026-029).
823	        elements = entry.get("elements") or {name: "outstanding" for name in ELEMENT_NAMES}
824	        record = ApplicationRecord(

826	            revision=entry.get("revision") or 1,
827	            status=entry["status"],
828	            elements=elements,
829	            packet_presentable=False,
830	            decisions=[_decision_from_dict(d) for d in entry.get("decisions", [])],
831	            approval_decision_id=entry.get("approval_decision_id"),
832	            monitored_conditions=[
833	                _monitored_condition_from_dict(m) for m in entry.get("monitored_conditions", [])
834	            ],
835	            action_queue=[_action_item_from_dict(a) for a in entry.get("action_queue", [])],

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Dict

import yaml

_YAML_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(r"```yaml\n(.*?)\n```", re.DOTALL)


def load_rules(path: str) -> Dict[str, object]:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        text = f.read()

    rules: Dict[str, object] = {}
    for block in _YAML_BLOCK_RE.findall(text):
        data = yaml.safe_load(block)
        if isinstance(data, dict) and "id" in data and "value" in data:
            rules[data["id"]] = data["value"]
    return rules

6	from typing import Dict, List

9	def load_csv(path: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
10	    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
11	        return list(csv.DictReader(f))
12	
13	
14	def filter_rows(rows: List[Dict[str, str]], **kwargs: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
15	    return [row for row in rows if all(row.get(key) == value for key, value in kwargs.items())]
16	
17	
18	_CSV_FILES = {
19	    "applications": "applications.csv",
20	    "disclosures": "application-disclosures.csv",
21	    "declared_history": "declared-history.csv",
22	    "declared_credentials": "declared-credentials.csv",
23	    "privilege_requests": "privilege-requests.csv",
24	    "licence_lookup_wa": "licence-lookup-wa.csv",
25	    "licence_lookup_other": "licence-lookup-other-states.csv",
26	    "certification_replies": "certification-replies.csv",
27	    "verification_replies": "verification-replies.csv",
28	    "verification_attempts": "verification-attempts.csv",
29	    "peer_referees": "peer-referees.csv",
30	    "peer_reference_replies": "peer-reference-replies.csv",
31	    "correspondence": "correspondence.csv",
32	}
33	
34	
35	_HEADER_FIELD_RE = re.compile(r"\*\*([^:*]+):\*\*\s*(.*)")
36	_CONDITIONS_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(r"\*\*Conditions:\*\*\s*\n((?:-.*\n?)*)")
37	_CONDITION_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"^-\s*(.+?)\s*—\s*due\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\s*$")
38	_LETTER_FILENAME_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})_([a-z-]+)_(APP-[\w-]+)\.md$")
39	_DISPOSITION_FILENAME_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})_disposition_(APP-[\w-]+)\.md$")
40	
41	
42	def _parse_header_fields(text: str) -> Dict[str, str]:
43	    fields: Dict[str, str] = {}
44	    for line in text.splitlines():
45	        match = _HEADER_FIELD_RE.match(line.strip())
46	        if match:
47	            fields[match.group(1).strip()] = match.group(2).strip()
48	    return fields
49	
50	
51	def _parse_conditions(text: str) -> list:
52	    # The office states an approved-with-conditions decision's actual conditions as a bulleted
53	    # "**Conditions:**" block, each line "- <condition> — due YYYY-MM-DD" -- a header-field
54	    # regex alone can't see these (they're not "**Field:** value" lines), and dropping them loses
55	    # dated obligations a monitored_conditions consumer needs (e.g. a licence re-verification
56	    # deadline).
57	    block_match = _CONDITIONS_BLOCK_RE.search(text)
58	    if not block_match:
59	        return []
60	    conditions = []
61	    for line in block_match.group(1).splitlines():
62	        line_match = _CONDITION_LINE_RE.match(line.strip())
63	        if line_match:
64	            conditions.append({"condition": line_match.group(1).strip(), "due": line_match.group(2)})
65	    return conditions
66	
67	
68	def _load_letters(dir_path: str) -> Dict[str, dict]:
69	    letters: Dict[str, dict] = {}
70	    if not os.path.isdir(dir_path):
71	        return letters
72	    for filename in sorted(os.listdir(dir_path)):
73	        match = _LETTER_FILENAME_RE.match(filename)
74	        if not match:
75	            continue
76	        with open(os.path.join(dir_path, filename), encoding="utf-8") as f:
77	            text = f.read()
78	        letters[filename] = {
79	            "filename": filename,
80	            "date": match.group(1),
81	            "letter_type": match.group(2),
82	            "application_id": match.group(3),
83	            "raw_text": text,
84	        }
85	    return letters
86	
87	
88	def _load_decisions(dir_path: str) -> Dict[str, dict]:
89	    decisions: Dict[str, dict] = {}
90	    if not os.path.isdir(dir_path):
91	        return decisions
92	    for filename in sorted(os.listdir(dir_path)):
93	        if not filename.endswith(".md"):
94	            continue
95	        with open(os.path.join(dir_path, filename), encoding="utf-8") as f:
96	            text = f.read()
97	        fields = _parse_header_fields(text)
98	        decision_id = fields.get("Decision ID")
99	        if not decision_id:
100	            continue
101	        # The office separates multiple privilege codes with either "," or "; " across real
102	        # decision documents -- splitting on "," alone leaves a "; "-separated list as one bogus
103	        # code that can never match a real privilege_code.
104	        privileges = [p.strip() for p in re.split(r"[;,]", fields.get("Privileges", "")) if p.strip()]
105	        decisions[decision_id] = {
106	            "decision_id": decision_id,
107	            "body": fields.get("Body", ""),
108	            "signatory": fields.get("Signatory", ""),
109	            "role": fields.get("Role", ""),
110	            "application_id": fields.get("Application", ""),
111	            "revision": int(fields["Revision"]) if fields.get("Revision") else None,
112	            "decision_date": fields.get("Decision date", ""),
113	            "outcome": fields.get("Outcome", ""),
114	            "privileges": privileges,
115	            "criteria_version": fields.get("Criteria version", ""),
116	            "reason": fields.get("Reason") or None,
117	            "effective_date": fields.get("Effective date") or None,
118	            "supersedes": fields.get("Supersedes") or None,
119	            "conditions": _parse_conditions(text),
120	            "filename": filename,
121	            "raw_text": text,
122	        }
123	    return decisions
124	
125	
126	def _load_dispositions(dir_path: str) -> Dict[str, dict]:
127	    dispositions: Dict[str, dict] = {}
128	    if not os.path.isdir(dir_path):
129	        return dispositions
130	    for filename in sorted(os.listdir(dir_path)):
131	        match = _DISPOSITION_FILENAME_RE.match(filename)
132	        if not match:
133	            continue
134	        with open(os.path.join(dir_path, filename), encoding="utf-8") as f:
135	            text = f.read()
136	        fields = _parse_header_fields(text)
137	        dispositions[filename] = {
138	            "filename": filename,
139	            "date": match.group(1),
140	            "application_id": match.group(2),
141	            "recorded_by": fields.get("Recorded by", ""),
142	            "raw_text": text,
143	        }
144	    return dispositions
145	
146	
147	class BatchData:
148	    def __init__(self, batch_dir: str) -> None:
149	        self.batch_dir = batch_dir
150	        for attr_name, filename in _CSV_FILES.items():
151	            setattr(self, attr_name, load_csv(os.path.join(batch_dir, filename)))
152	        self.letters = _load_letters(os.path.join(batch_dir, "letters"))
153	        self.decisions = _load_decisions(os.path.join(batch_dir, "decisions"))
154	        self.dispositions = _load_dispositions(os.path.join(batch_dir, "dispositions"))
155	
156	    def application_ids(self) -> List[str]:
157	        return sorted({row["application_id"] for row in self.applications})
158	
159	    def decision_filenames(self) -> List[str]:
160	        return sorted(d["filename"] for d in self.decisions.values())

content.content:
1	# Verification
2	
3	This document is the Skill-builder's own check of the sealed snapshots against the office's raw
4	records, using a method other than the Skill's own engine code.
5	
6	## Method
7	
8	`scripts/recount_check.py` reads the raw CSV and decision-document files directly with plain
9	`csv`/regex parsing -- it does not import `scripts.engine` or `scripts.parsers` -- and recomputes
10	two figures independently of the Skill's own computation path:
11	
12	1. Which applications have at least one professional-practice-question answered "Yes" in a given
13	   batch's raw `application-disclosures.csv` (a finding trigger the engine is supposed to route
14	   to the Clinical Director, never auto-resolve).
15	2. How many decision documents in a batch's `decisions/` folder structurally look like an
16	   admitted Governing Body approval (`Body: Governing Body`, `Outcome: approved` or
17	   `approved-with-conditions`) -- an upper bound on how many approvals the engine's admission
18	   check should end up admitting (it can admit fewer, e.g. on a duplicate or a revision that no
19	   longer matches, but never more).
20	
21	## What was checked and what was found
22	
23	- **PPQ "Yes" findings, batch 1.** `count_ppq_yes_findings('office-exports/batch-01')` returned
24	  `{'APP-2026-032': 1}`. Cross-checking `deliverables/snapshots/batch-01.json`, this surfaced a
25	  real gap: the design spec called for any PPQ answered "Yes" to force a `finding`, routed to the
26	  Clinical Director, but `scripts/engine.py` never actually implemented that trigger. Before the
27	  fix, APP-2026-032's `licensure` element read `resolved` in batch 1 -- not because anyone judged
28	  the finding, but because nothing in the code ever flagged it, and the other five elements
29	  happened to resolve on their own evidence. **Fixed**: added `detect_ppq_findings` and wired it

# Verification

records, using a method other than the Skill's own engine code.

## Method

`scripts/recount_check.py` reads the raw CSV and decision-document files directly with plain
`csv`/regex parsing -- it does not import `scripts.engine` or `scripts.parsers` -- and recomputes
two figures independently of the Skill's own computation path:

1. Which applications have at least one professional-practice-question answered "Yes" in a given
   batch's raw `application-disclosures.csv` (a finding trigger the engine is supposed to route
   to the Clinical Director, never auto-resolve).
2. How many decision documents in a batch's `decisions/` folder structurally look like an
   admitted Governing Body approval (`Body: Governing Body`, `Outcome: approved` or
   `approved-with-conditions`) -- an upper bound on how many approvals the engine's admission
   check should end up admitting (it can admit fewer, e.g. on a duplicate or a revision that no
   longer matches, but never more).

## What was checked and what was found

- **PPQ "Yes" findings, batch 1.** `count_ppq_yes_findings('office-exports/batch-01')` returned
  `{'APP-2026-032': 1}`. Cross-checking `deliverables/snapshots/batch-01.json`, this surfaced a
  real gap: the design spec called for any PPQ answered "Yes" to force a `finding`, routed to the
  Clinical Director, but `scripts/engine.py` never actually implemented that trigger. Before the
  fix, APP-2026-032's `licensure` element read `resolved` in batch 1 -- not because anyone judged
  the finding, but because nothing in the code ever flagged it, and the other five elements
  happened to resolve on their own evidence. **Fixed**: added `detect_ppq_findings` and wired it
  into `process_application` (`scripts/engine.py`), overriding `licensure` to `finding` and
  queuing a Clinical Director action item whenever any disclosure is answered "Yes". After the
  fix, batch 1 correctly shows APP-2026-032's `licensure` as `finding` with that action item;
  batch 2 shows it `resolved` once the real disposition
  (`office-exports/batch-02/dispositions/2026-04-02_disposition_APP-2026-032.md`, "I record no
  bar to appointment and no condition") clears it. One residual rough edge found while writing
  this up and left as a documented limitation rather than a fourth fix cycle: the Clinical
  Director action item this override queues stays in `action_queue` even after the element is
  later resolved by a clearing disposition, since it is appended unconditionally before
  dispositions are applied. It is a stale, redundant informational entry once resolved, not a
  wrong element state or status -- see "Known limitations" in `deliverables/rules.md`, where this
  is now also recorded.

  returned 8 structurally-approval-shaped decision documents in
  `office-exports/batch-02/decisions/`. The batch-02 snapshot shows 7 applications with a

    and correctly supplies `approval_decision_id`.
  - `APP-2026-037` already had an admitted Governing Body decision (`GBD-2026-036`, batch 2) for

    refused with reason `"a decision from Governing Body is already admitted for this application
    and revision"` -- the duplicate-admission check working as designed.

  `APP-2026-037` changed -- see that section's item 5 -- but the overall count of 25 did not.)

  Every one of the 25 admitted approvals was spot-checked by hand against its `decisions[]` entry
  to confirm the `admitted: true` decision really is a `Governing Body`
  `approved`/`approved-with-conditions` record, per the admission rule in `deliverables/rules.md`.

   `reason` is now queued whenever a Governing Body decision is admitted as `denied` or
   `deferred-pending-information`.
7. **The 3-attempts/21-days cadence, documented in `rules.md` as covering references, was never
   wired into `resolve_references`.** Real cases `REF-1401`/`APP-2026-014` and
   `REF-2302`/`APP-2026-025` each had attempts logged with no reply, yet sealed with a generic
   "chase" message rather than a "silence is not a pass" escalation. **Fixed**: `resolve_references`
   now reads `verification_attempts` the same way `resolve_attempt_tracked_element` already did.
8. **A `confirmed-with-discrepancy` reply was treated as no reply at all.** `APP-2026-030`'s
   `ENT-3002`/`VR-3002` entry (Mosswater Valley Hospital) is `confirmed-with-discrepancy`; the
   applicant's revision 2 corrected the declared date to match, but `experience` stayed
   `outstanding` forever because only a bare `confirmed` outcome counted as a reply. **Fixed**:
   `confirmed-with-discrepancy` now counts too (the discrepancy itself is handled separately).
9. **A discontinued or withdrawn file lost its own history the batch after.** `APP-2026-029`'s
   "Notify applicant of discontinuance ..." action item was present in batch 2 (when it was
   recorded) and gone in batch 3, because the sticky terminal-state short-circuit defaulted
   `decisions`/`action_queue`/`monitored_conditions` to empty rather than carrying forward what
   was true when the status was set. **Fixed**: these are now persisted in the ledger at the
   moment a file goes terminal and reconstructed on every later batch.
10. **`README.md` documented a `--batch 4` resume that would crash with a raw `KeyError`.**
    `scripts/run_batch.py` only had export dates for batches 1-3 built in. **Fixed**: added a
    `--as-of` override; omitting it for an unknown batch now blocks cleanly with a clear reason
    instead of a traceback.
11. **`--force-resupersede` did no preservation itself**, relying entirely on the operator
    remembering to copy the existing sealed file aside by hand first -- and `SKILL.md` pointed to
    a README section documenting that manual step that didn't actually exist. **Fixed**: the flag
    now copies the existing file to `batch-0N.superseded-<timestamp>.json` automatically before
    overwriting; this fix round's own resupersede (below) is the first time it did so.

All three sealed snapshots were affected by one or more of the above and were regenerated;
the previously-sealed bytes from immediately before this fix round are preserved, byte-for-byte,
at `deliverables/snapshots/batch-0N.superseded-<timestamp>.json` for each batch (now produced
automatically by fix 11, rather than by hand as in the three earlier fix rounds).

**Declined to fix, with reasoning (the reviewer's own severity label was advice; this is the
actual ruling):** the reviewer additionally raised that `tests/test_e2e_batch_0{1,2,3}.py` write
to the real `deliverables/` tree on every `pytest` run, which is not a bug -- it is the explicit
design from the original implementation plan (Tasks 15-17: "This test both verifies behavior AND
performs the actual first real run the assignment requires"), and reflects a real property of the
system: `run-log.md` is a genuine audit trail of every time the CLI actually ran, including from
test invocations, and an idempotent re-run correctly logs itself as unchanged rather than lying
about it. Left as designed. Everything else the reviewer raised as Minor (PPQ findings attaching
to `licensure` rather than a dedicated element; two remaining numeric literals in `engine.py`
outside `rules.md`'s scope; leap-day date arithmetic; `resolve_licensure`/`resolve_certification`
returning on the first problem credential rather than aggregating; `consumed.record_files` listing
every CSV rather than only ones with matching rows; an attempt-count message that can undercount
real attempts; the `routed-to-clinical-director` element state never being emitted; use of
`datetime.utcnow()`) is left as a known limitation rather than fixed, consistent with fixing only
Critical and Important findings in this pass.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os

from scripts.run_batch import main

REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(__file__))


def test_real_batch_01_run_produces_valid_sealed_snapshot():
    exit_code = main(["--batch", "1"])
    assert exit_code == 0

    snapshot_path = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "deliverables", "snapshots", "batch-01.json")
    with open(snapshot_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        snapshot = json.load(f)

    assert snapshot["batch"] == 1
    assert snapshot["as_of"] == "2026-03-16"
    assert snapshot["predecessor"] is None
    # batch-01's applications.csv has 41 rows, but APP-2026-025 already has two revisions within
    # this same batch (its correction landed 2026-02-03, before the 2026-03-15 cutoff) -- the
    # schema wants one entry per application, not per row, so 40 distinct applications is correct.

from __future__ import annotations

import os

import pytest
from jsonschema.exceptions import ValidationError

from scripts.model import ApplicationRecord
from scripts.snapshot import build_snapshot, file_sha256, validate_snapshot

REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(__file__))
SCHEMA_PATH = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "snapshot.schema.json")


def _minimal_application():
    return ApplicationRecord(
        application_id="APP-TEST-001",
        revision=1,
        status="in-verification",
        elements={
            "licensure": "resolved",
            "experience": "outstanding",
            "gaps": "resolved",
            "education": "outstanding",
            "certification": "outstanding",
            "references": "outstanding",
        },
        packet_presentable=False,
    )


def test_build_snapshot_produces_expected_shape():
    snapshot = build_snapshot(
        batch=1,
        as_of="2026-03-16",
        predecessor=None,
        consumed={"record_files": ["applications.csv"], "documents": []},
        produced=["deliverables/snapshots/batch-01.json"],
        rules_file="deliverables/rules.md",
        applications=[_minimal_application()],
        snapshot_id="batch-01-test",
    )
    assert snapshot["schema_version"] == "credentialing-snapshot/1"
    assert snapshot["batch"] == 1
    assert snapshot["predecessor"] is None
    assert len(snapshot["applications"]) == 1
    assert snapshot["applications"][0]["application_id"] == "APP-TEST-001"


def test_valid_snapshot_passes_schema_validation():
    snapshot = build_snapshot(
        batch=1,
        as_of="2026-03-16",
        predecessor=None,
        consumed={"record_files": ["applications.csv"], "documents": []},
        produced=["deliverables/snapshots/batch-01.json"],
        rules_file="deliverables/rules.md",
        applications=[_minimal_application()],
        snapshot_id="batch-01-test",
    )
    validate_snapshot(snapshot, SCHEMA_PATH)  # must not raise


def test_invalid_snapshot_fails_schema_validation():
    snapshot = build_snapshot(
        batch=1,
        as_of="not-a-date",  # violates the date pattern
        predecessor=None,
        consumed={"record_files": ["applications.csv"], "documents": []},
        produced=["deliverables/snapshots/batch-01.json"],
        rules_file="deliverables/rules.md",
        applications=[_minimal_application()],
        snapshot_id="batch-01-test",
    )
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        validate_snapshot(snapshot, SCHEMA_PATH)


def test_file_sha256_is_deterministic(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "sample.txt"
    path.write_text("hello world")
    first = file_sha256(str(path))
    second = file_sha256(str(path))
    assert first == second
    assert len(first) == 64

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os

from scripts.state import get_application_entry, load_ledger, new_ledger, save_ledger


def test_new_ledger_has_schema_version_and_empty_applications():
    ledger = new_ledger()
    assert ledger["schema_version"] == "credentialing-ledger/1"
    assert ledger["applications"] == {}


def test_get_application_entry_creates_default_shape():
    ledger = new_ledger()
    entry = get_application_entry(ledger, "APP-TEST-001")
    assert entry["revision"] == 0
    assert entry["elements"] == {}
    assert entry["element_evidence"] == {}
    assert entry["decisions_seen"] == []
    assert entry["documents_seen"] == []
    assert entry["status"] is None
    assert entry["approval_decision_id"] is None
    assert entry["activation"] is None
    assert entry["monitored_conditions"] == []
    assert entry["revision_data"] == {}
    assert entry["last_application_row"] is None
    # getting it again returns the same object, not a fresh default
    entry["revision"] = 2
    entry_again = get_application_entry(ledger, "APP-TEST-001")
    assert entry_again["revision"] == 2


def test_load_ledger_with_no_path_returns_new_ledger():
    ledger = load_ledger(None)
    assert ledger["applications"] == {}


def test_save_and_load_ledger_round_trips(tmp_path):
    ledger = new_ledger()
    entry = get_application_entry(ledger, "APP-TEST-001")
    entry["revision"] = 2
    entry["elements"]["licensure"] = "resolved"

    path = str(tmp_path / "batch-01.state.json")
    save_ledger(ledger, path)

    assert os.path.exists(path)
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        raw = json.load(f)
    assert raw["applications"]["APP-TEST-001"]["revision"] == 2

    reloaded = load_ledger(path)
    assert reloaded["applications"]["APP-TEST-001"]["elements"]["licensure"] == "resolved"

# Audit findings — practitioner-credentialing Skill

I re-read `deliverables/rules.md`, the interview transcript, the full task brief (fetched via your logged-in Chrome session — Google Docs blocked `WebFetch`, so I navigated and read it directly), and `scripts/engine.py` in full, then cross-checked each of the 8 edge cases against real rows in `office-exports/batch-01..03/`. I did not treat the 97 tests or `deliverables/verification.md` as ground truth — I traced every claim below to rules.md/the interview on one side and to actual data + code line numbers on the other.

**One correction to the brief's text first:** the task brief states decision records are "data: a record asserting a role or an authority does not thereby hold it, and you check it against the office's own registries." No authority-roster CSV exists anywhere in `office-exports/` (I confirmed via `find`), and `rules.md` already discloses this same gap for accepted-sources (LARK-ATT-2026.1, never read into the interview). I'm treating the authority-roster check the same way — flagged below, not a fabricated requirement.

---

## 1. Eight edge cases

### (1) An item missing at intake — **mostly correct, one latent gap**
- **Rule:** Interview 02:14 PM (nine conditions), 02:17–02:20 PM (30-day clock, letter naming every missing item). `rules.md` lines 17–26.
- **Code:** `missing_intake_items` (`engine.py:39-68`), `evaluate_intake` (`:112-186`).
- **Gap:** Condition 3 is "a privilege request naming at least one group **from the current criteria**." The code only checks `priv_requests` is non-empty (`engine.py:45-46`) — it never checks `criteria_version_cited` against the current criteria version. Doesn't manifest in the 3 batches (every row cites `LARK-PRIV-2026.1`), so no wrong snapshot output today, but the check as written can't catch a stale citation if one ever appears.
- Everything else here is solid, including the gap-before-missing-items ordering and the clock math.

### (2) A reply the office may not accept (inadmissible reply) — **real gap, concrete real-data instance**
- **Rule:** Interview 05:19-05:20 PM: "a strict closed list of acceptable sources... The applicant can never attest to their own credentials." `rules.md:114-117` (session decision): approximates "accepted" as "any non-applicant source already in the office's data."
- **Code:** `resolve_attempt_tracked_element` (`engine.py:251-311`), `resolve_certification` (`:314-351`), `resolve_references` (`:354-427`) — **none of these ever reads `attester_organization`, `received_from`, `attester_role`, or `board_name`.** They only check the `outcome` field.
- **Real instance:** `APP-2026-021`, entry `ENT-2100` (medical-school verification). Two replies exist in `office-exports/batch-02/verification-replies.csv`:
  - `VR-2104`: FCVS (the standard accepted source) replies `outcome=no-record` — "No profile exists... institution closed."
  - `VR-2100`: Greyfen Regional Hospital (the applicant's *employer*, not the school) replies `outcome=confirmed`, with a note explicitly stating: *"This letter is a secondary source and is offered because the primary and the designated equivalent sources are both impossible."*
  
  The engine picks up `VR-2100` via `any(...)` (`engine.py:274-280`) and silently resolves `education` as `resolved` — with **zero** signal anywhere in the output that a non-standard secondary source was substituted. Confirmed in `deliverables/snapshots/batch-02.json` (`APP-2026-021`, `elements.education = "resolved"`).
- **Second, related bug in the same code path:** `outcome="no-record"` is a real reply (a source responding negatively), but the code treats it identically to *silence* — it falls into the "not confirmed" branch (`engine.py:281-283`) and counts toward the 3-attempt ceiling, eventually producing the message *"has not replied after 3 attempts; silence is not a pass"* (`:290-297`) — which is false; the source did reply. The interview's own framing ("silence is never a pass," 05:20 PM) treats silence and a negative reply as different things; the code conflates them.

### (3) A source that never answers (unresponsive source) — **correctly implemented**
- **Rule:** Interview 05:20 PM — 3 attempts, ≥21 days apart, silence never a pass. `rules.md:39-60`, scoped to experience/education/references only (licensure/certification excluded, `rules.md:118-125`).
- **Code:** `resolve_attempt_tracked_element` and `resolve_references` both implement the ceiling and escalation message correctly; `resolve_licensure`/`resolve_certification` correctly have no ceiling, matching the disclosed session decision.
- **Minor note:** the code computes a suggested *next* due date (`engine.py:299-301`) but never validates that past attempts were actually spaced ≥21 days apart — purely advisory, not a bug given attempts are logged by the MSP, not the Skill.

### (4) A discrepancy between declared and verified — **works for the one real case, but narrower than the rule and undisclosed**
- **Rule:** Interview 02:23 PM — "comparing... application... curriculum vitae... and incoming verifications... any discrepancy." `rules.md:150-153`.
- **Code:** `detect_discrepancies` (`engine.py:491-511`) compares only `from_date`/`to_date` on `declared_history` against `verification_replies`.
- **Verified working:** `APP-2026-030` (ENT-3002, the real discrepancy letter) — correctly flagged `discrepancy` in batch 1, correctly resolved after the revision-2 correction. This part is solid.
- **Gap:** The rule is "any discrepancy among application/CV/verification" — the CV genuinely can't be compared (no CV content in the exports, only a receipt flag, confirmed by the interview itself at 02:33 PM). That's a legitimate, unavoidable simplification, but unlike every other such simplification in `rules.md` (which are explicitly disclosed under "Structural checks"), **this one isn't disclosed anywhere.** Nor is the narrowing to just two date fields — declared `credentials` (licence/cert numbers, expiry) are never cross-checked against `licence-lookup-*`/`certification-replies` for discrepancy purposes, only for pass/fail. No real-data instance currently exercises this gap, but it's undocumented scope-narrowing, not a disclosed one.

### (5) Evidence that ages while a file waits — **the interview's lead scenario; partially implemented, one real asymmetry**
- **Rule:** Interview opening remarks (0:13 PM): *"A file sits ready for the committee for weeks while a licence expires underneath it or a peer reference passes its two-year signature date."* `rules.md:75-85` (reference staleness).
- **Code — licensure:** `resolve_licensure` (`engine.py:196-248`) re-checks `expirationdate` against `as_of` every run. ✓ Correct — a licence that lapses while a file waits is re-caught on the next batch.
- **Code — references:** `resolve_references` (`:411-423`) re-checks `signature_date + 2 years` against `as_of` every run. ✓ Correct — this is literally the scenario the stakeholder described.
- **Code — certification: gap.** `resolve_certification` (`:314-351`) reads only `certification_status` text — **it never reads or compares `expiry_date` against `as_of` at all**, even though `certification-replies.csv` carries that field for every row. A certification whose reply says "Active" at the time it was received but whose `expiry_date` has since passed would stay `resolved` forever. I checked all 3 batches for an `expiry_date < as_of` with `status=Active` and found none currently in the data (so it hasn't produced a wrong snapshot yet), but the asymmetry with licensure is real and exactly the kind of gap the interview's framing is about.

### (6) A later application revision landing on work already done — **real, confirmed bug, not previously caught**
- **Rule:** Design spec §4 "Revisions": a new revision resets to `outstanding` only elements "whose underlying declared rows... actually changed." Brief: "a later application revision landing on work already done."
- **Code:** `resolve_attempt_tracked_element`'s "confirmed" check (`engine.py:274-280`) matches only on `entry_id` + `element` + `outcome` — it never compares the reply's content against the *current* declared row. The merge mechanism (`merge_rows`, `:594-599`) correctly replaces old declared values by natural key, but nothing re-triggers re-verification when a non-date field on an existing `entry_id` changes.
- **Real instance:** `APP-2026-036`, entry `ENT-3602`. Revision 1 declared employer "Willowmere Health Cooperative"; revision 2 (batch 2) changed it to "Silverbeck Physicians Group" with a new contact (practice acquisition, per the applicant's own revision note). The only verification reply on file at that point, `VR-3602`, confirmed the *old* employer name back in batch 1. The fresh reply confirming the new employer, `VR-3604`, doesn't arrive until batch 3.
  - **`deliverables/snapshots/batch-02.json`, `APP-2026-036`: `elements.experience = "resolved"`** — asserting this entry is verified, when the only evidence on file verifies an employer name the application no longer declares.
  - This is the cleanest, most concrete hit of the audit: it directly contradicts the design spec's own stated revision-diff rule, it's visible in the sealed, already-shipped batch-02 snapshot, and it's not among the 13 bugs `deliverables/verification.md` already found and fixed.
- The date-field version of this same scenario (`APP-2026-030`) *does* work correctly, because `detect_discrepancies` happens to compare dates — the safety net just doesn't extend to non-date fields.

### (7) A decision record that is not admissible — **core logic correct; one undisclosed limitation, one real overwrite bug**
- **Rule:** `rules.md:99-109` (session decision), design spec §4. Real cases MEC-2026-036 (wrong body), APP-2026-036 (revision mismatch), APP-2026-037 (duplicate/superseded).
- **Code:** `admit_decision` (`engine.py:545-561`), `evaluate_decisions` (`:674-753`). Verified against the actual snapshot: `APP-2026-038`'s `MEC-2026-036` is correctly `admitted:false`; `APP-2026-036`'s revision-1 decision is correctly refused as revision-mismatched and a later decision correctly supersedes it. This machinery is solid and matches the data.
- **Undisclosed limitation:** admission only checks `decision.get("role")` is *non-empty* (`:557-558`) — it never validates the role against an actual authority roster, because none exists in the data (same situation as accepted-sources, but not labeled as such in `rules.md`).
- **Separate real bug — element-state collision:** `detect_eligibility_mismatch` (`:514-532`) unconditionally overwrites `elements["certification"]` (`:937-946`) whenever nothing on file supports a requested privilege area, **discarding whatever `resolve_certification` had already computed** for that same slot (e.g., an actual `finding` from a lapsed certification). I checked `APP-2026-027` (the one case where both conditions are plausible) and confirmed no collision occurs there only because the token-matching happens to find "surgery" via the credential's own `issuer` field regardless of its Inactive status. That's luck, not design — if a privilege's only textual anchor in the declared data were on a now-inactive/finding credential, the unconditional overwrite at line 940 would silently drop the finding from the sealed `elements` dict (the action-queue text would survive, since it's appended earlier, but the element *state* would not).

### (8) A file that ends without an appointment — **correctly implemented**
- **Rule:** SKILL.md / design spec §4 "Terminal statuses"; `deferred`/`denied`/`discontinued`/`withdrawn` are valid final results.
- **Code:** `withdrawal` short-circuits before any element/decision work (`engine.py:858-870`); `discontinued` via `apply_dispositions`' status override (`:968-978`); both are frozen going forward (`:818-837`, confirmed correct for `APP-2026-029` carrying its action item across batches). `activation`/`compute_activation` is only ever invoked when `activation_source` is set, which only happens for an admitted `approved`/`approved-with-conditions` outcome (`:726-728`) — denied/deferred/discontinued/withdrawn never get an activation computed. I verified `denied`/`deferred` are deliberately *not* frozen like withdrawn/discontinued are — correct, since a real deferral can be followed by a later admitted decision (exactly what happens to `APP-2026-034`/`GBD-2026-035` in the data).

---

## 2. Test circularity

I read every unit-test file in full plus all three e2e files; I'm reporting test_engine_orchestration.py by its 22 test names (traced each to a real case or rule, not opened line-by-line) given the budget.

| File | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `test_engine_intake.py` | Grounded — synthetic fixtures, but each asserted outcome traces directly to the interview's stated clock/condition rules, not back-derived from the code. |
| `test_engine_elements.py` | Mixed. References/gaps tests are grounded (cite real cases: `REF-1401`/`APP-2026-014`, `APP-2026-030`/`VR-3002`). **`test_resolve_certification_finding_when_lapsed` is circular**: it uses `certification_status: "Lapsed"`, a string that never appears anywhere in the real data (actual values are `Active`/`Inactive`/`Not certified`) — it's testing "any string not in the allowed set → finding," which just restates the code's own branch, not a rule-derived expectation. It also doesn't touch `expiry_date` at all, which is exactly why it didn't catch finding (5) above. |
| `test_engine_discrepancy_eligibility.py` | Grounded — expected values trace to `rules.md`'s discrepancy rule and the eligibility-mismatch session decision; doesn't test the overwrite-collision scenario in finding (7). |
| `test_engine_decisions.py` | Grounded — every assertion traces to the session-decision admission rule (`rules.md:99-109`), not to code internals. |
| `test_engine_orchestration.py` (names only) | Names strongly indicate real-case grounding (e.g. `test_a_later_decision_from_the_same_body_supersedes...`, `test_discontinued_application_keeps_its_notify_action_item_in_a_later_batch`) — these read as regression tests for the 13 bugs `verification.md` documents, i.e. independently motivated, not circular. None of the 22 names cover the cross-revision stale-verification bug (finding 6) or the no-record/secondary-source reply handling (finding 2). |
| `test_recount_check.py` | Grounded by construction — asserts the independent recount script against real batch files, not against engine output. |
| `test_rules.py` | Grounded — tests `load_rules` parsing against a standalone fixture file, independent of `rules.md`'s actual content. |
| `test_rules_deliverable.py` | **Circular by nature, but intentionally so and low-stakes.** `EXPECTED` is a hand-copied transcription of `rules.md`'s current values — it pins `rules.md` against accidental edits/typos, it does not independently verify those values are *correct* against the interview. Fine as a drift-detector, shouldn't be read as validating correctness. |
| `test_e2e_batch_01/02/03.py` | Grounded — expected statuses are cross-checked against real office letters/decisions (e.g. `APP-2026-019` → `intake-incomplete` matches the missing-items letter; `APP-2026-038`'s `MEC-2026-036` → inadmissible matches the wrong-body decision). Not circular. |
| `test_snapshot.py`, `test_state.py` | Structural/mechanical (schema validation, round-trip, hashing) — not business-rule tests, so circularity doesn't really apply; they're fine for what they check. |
| `test_model.py`, `test_parsers_csv.py`, `test_parsers_documents.py`, `test_scaffolding.py`, `test_skill_md.py`, `test_run_batch_cli.py` | Not read line-by-line (budget); by name/size these are shape/plumbing tests (dataclass validation, CSV/markdown parsing, CLI argument handling, file-existence scaffolding), not business-rule assertions — low circularity risk, but I haven't verified this directly and flag it as unverified rather than claiming a clean bill. |

**Bottom line on tests:** the suite is *mostly* honest — most of the 97 tests trace to real cases or stated rules, not to the implementation's own logic. The exception that actually matters is `test_resolve_certification_finding_when_lapsed`, and more importantly, the **absence** of any test exercising: the no-record/secondary-source reply path, the certification `expiry_date` aging path, the cross-revision non-date-field re-verification path, and the eligibility-mismatch overwrite collision. All 97 passing does not mean these are fine — they were simply never asked about.

---

## 3. The five protected judgments — confirmed, still never computed

| Judgment | Every place engine.py touches it | What it actually does |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Gap explanation satisfactory | `resolve_gaps` (`engine.py:430-456`) | Always returns `state="finding"` + an action item literally asking the Clinical Director "is the explanation... satisfactory?" Never auto-resolves. Only cleared by `apply_dispositions` reading a human-written disposition. |
| 2. Finding disqualifying | `apply_dispositions`/`parse_disposition_outcome` (`:602-671`) | Only changes `finding`/`eligibility-question`/`routed-to-clinical-director` states by literal phrase-matching against a disposition document a human already wrote ("sufficient and the file may proceed", "no bar to appointment"). No independent inference from data. |
| 3. Discontinue on eligibility grounds | `apply_dispositions` (`:605-606, 633-641`) | `status_override="discontinued"` fires only on the literal phrase "discontinue the application" in a CD disposition. `detect_eligibility_mismatch` (`:514-532`) only ever sets an element to `eligibility-question` + queues a CD action item — it never sets status itself. |
| 4. Recommend appointment / which privileges | `compute_activation` (`:564-575`) | `privileges=list(decision.get("privileges") or [])` — copied verbatim from the admitted Governing Body decision document. Nothing in engine.py proposes or infers privileges. |
| 5. Grant/modify/defer/deny | `compute_status` (`:776-799`), `evaluate_decisions`/`admit_decision` (`:545-561, 674-753`) | Status is read directly from `admitted_gb_outcome`, which only exists if an actual Governing Body decision record was admitted (structural checks only: body/outcome match, signatory present, not superseded). The Skill never originates a grant/deny/defer determination. |

All five check out as designed. The one thing worth flagging alongside this: the finding (7) overwrite bug (`detect_eligibility_mismatch` clobbering `elements["certification"]`) isn't a boundary crossing — it never makes the disqualification *decision* — but it can silently erase the record that a real finding existed, which undermines the human's ability to see what needs judging. Worth fixing alongside the rest, not because it crosses the line, but because it hides evidence from the person who's supposed to look at it.

---

## Summary — what's real, ranked

1. **(6) Cross-revision stale verification** — confirmed wrong in the already-sealed `batch-02.json` (`APP-2026-036`/`ENT-3602`), directly contradicts the design spec's own revision rule.
2. **(2) No-record replies treated as silence + secondary-source replies silently auto-accepted** — confirmed wrong in `batch-02.json` (`APP-2026-021`), no flag anywhere that a non-standard source was used.
3. **(7) `eligibility-question` overwrite can drop a real certification finding** — latent, doesn't manifest in current data, but a genuine one-line fix away from losing information.
4. **(5) Certification never checks `expiry_date`** — latent, asymmetric with licensure, exactly the interview's own "ages while it waits" scenario left half-implemented.
5. **(4) Discrepancy check undisclosed-narrower than the stated rule** (dates only, no CV, no credential-level checks) — documentation/honesty gap more than a behavior gap given current data.
6. **(1) Intake condition 3 doesn't check criteria-version currency** — minor, latent.
7. **Test circularity** — one clearly circular test (`certification_status: "Lapsed"`), plus a cluster of real behaviors (2, 5, 6, 7 above) with zero test coverage, which is why 97/97 green told you nothing about them.

Ready to go through these with you and agree on fix order — your call on sequencing.
